evaluations.evidence: create a new game by entering a name and an optional description
evaluations.rationale: Specific, bounded creation action with clear inputs.

evaluations.evidence: invite estimators by giving them a URL where they can access the game
evaluations.rationale: Specific action with a clear mechanism and purpose.

evaluations.evidence: start a round by entering an item in a single multi-line text field
see all items we try to estimate this session
evaluations.rationale: Defined list display for the current session; not an overly broad capability.

evaluations.evidence: select an item to be estimated or re-estimated
evaluations.rationale: Clear selection behavior with limited scope.

evaluations.evidence: add an item to the list of items to be estimated
edit an item in the list of items to be estimated
delete an item from the list of items to be estimated
show all estimates immediately
accept the average of all estimates
have the estimate field filled in automatically if all estimators show the same card
enter the agreed-upon estimate
estimate a story we estimated earlier in the session again
import stories from a spreadsheet
evaluations.rationale: Defined import capability; implementation details can be estimated.

evaluations.evidence: copy/paste stories from a spreadsheet
browse through previous games
evaluations.rationale: Bounded navigation/listing behavior for existing games.

evaluations.evidence: view a transcript of a game
evaluations.rationale: Specific read-only view of stories and estimates.

evaluations.evidence: export a transcript of a game as a HTML file
export a transcript of a game as a CSV file
delete a game
create an account for the application by entering my name, email address, a password and a username
evaluations.rationale: Specific account creation with named fields.

evaluations.evidence: log in using my account name and password
change my account details
evaluations.rationale: Account details are established elsewhere in the backlog; scope is understandable.

evaluations.evidence: delete my account
see dates and times in my local timezone
get a password reminder by email
select whether to have the team estimate with {0, 1/2, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, etc.} or {0, 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, etc.}
evaluations.rationale: Explicit options and bounded selection behavior.

evaluations.evidence: invite up to 15 estimators
join a game by entering my name on the page I received the URL for
see the item we're estimating
see all items we will try to estimate this session
evaluations.rationale: Specific list view for session items.

evaluations.evidence: immediately see that an estimate has been given by a specific estimator
be shown all estimates at the same time after all estimators have given their estimate
be able to change my estimate up until the last person selects a card and all are shown
see each estimator's prior estimates for the story being estimated
see who gave what estimates during the current round
be able start a two-minute countdown timer that all participants can see
have the two-minute timer reset itself as soon as we all play an estimate
scroll back through the stories and estimates from prior rounds
always have the cards in the same order across multiple draws
change my estimate as long as the draw has not been completed
have a small thumbnail photo displayed near where my cards are played
written a site which is compliant with XHTML and CSS standards
evaluations.rationale: Cross-cutting compliance requirement over the entire site is coarse-grained and difficult to estimate.

evaluations.evidence: have a list of definitions for commonly used terms
have created database indexes, so that the queries run as fast as possible
evaluations.rationale: Unbounded performance-oriented database work; 'as fast as possible' is vague and makes estimation difficult.

evaluations.evidence: have the application function correctly in Internet Explorer 6 and 7, Firefox 1.5 and 2, and Safari 2
evaluations.rationale: Cross-browser compatibility across the whole application is broad and costly to estimate.

evaluations.evidence: comply with the W3C accessibility guidelines where possible
evaluations.rationale: Broad accessibility requirement with vague 'where possible' scope.

evaluations.evidence: have the application respond quickly to my actions
evaluations.rationale: Performance requirement lacks measurable target and applies across the application.

evaluations.evidence: be able to use Unicode
evaluations.rationale: Specific technical capability, although cross-cutting; can be reasonably estimated.

evaluations.evidence: see sensible and predictable URLs
evaluations.rationale: Vague wording, but URL design is bounded enough to estimate.

evaluations.evidence: have nice error pages when something goes wrong
evaluations.rationale: Specific error-page deliverable despite subjective wording.

evaluations.evidence: results to be stored in a non-identifiable way
evaluations.rationale: Anonymization/privacy scope is underspecified and broad, making implementation effort hard to estimate.

evaluations.evidence: see some metrics on use of the game
evaluations.rationale: Extremely vague 'some metrics' leaves scope too open to estimate.
